teaser.text: UnitedHealth Group sells health coverage and many of the services needed to deliver, administer and pay for healthcare. Its central economic task is to collect premiums and fees, pay for care and operations, and manage the risks and timing between those two events.

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $357.26 in October 2027, a 3% loss including dividends. It reaches $394.17 in October 2028, a 10% gain. By October 2029, it reaches $441.90, a 25% gain.
The bear endpoint is $256.44. The bull endpoint is $664.40. Today’s price is $377.76. The bear case carries a 30% probability, the base case 50%, and the bull case 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for UnitedHealth?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast implies a 3% loss including dividends in October 2027 and a 25% gain including dividends in October 2029. Bear, base and bull cases carry 30%, 50% and 20% probabilities. The recovery must align medical costs with pricing, move Optum Health toward its 6%–8% margin target, and let cash generation support investment and payouts. By December 31, 2026, prior authorization—insurer approval required before certain care or medicines—is committed to fall 30%. December’s 2027 outlook tests the recovery. Medicare compliance and tax disputes remain unresolved. The investment turns on whether scale becomes durable per-share earnings.

The bull case requires durable cost control, sound payments and documentation, stronger Optum Health risk-contract margins and cash generation sufficient to expand buybacks. It gives $439.34 in October 2027 and $664.40 in October 2029. Its 20% probability reflects the upside from execution, but also the absence of proof through a full pricing cycle.

blocks.heading: How much cash does UnitedHealth really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash flow was $19.7 billion in 2025, but UnitedHealth sold $3.0 billion of receivables and received the cash early. Excluding that acceleration gives a lower sensitivity measure. Capital also sits inside regulated insurance subsidiaries, where it must support claims and may not be freely transferred to the parent. Equity rose while operating return on equity weakened, so the capital table shows quantity without proving quality.

dividend.opening: UnitedHealth currently pays $2.32 per quarter, or $9.28 annually at four payments. Operating cash has funded dividends and buybacks, but payouts exceeded reported earnings in 2025.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains UnitedHealth's business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does UnitedHealth pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The current quarterly dividend is $2.32, implying $9.28 annually at four payments. The base path rises from $9.59 to $10.57 as the forecast allows a partial-year increase followed by roughly 5% annual growth. The bear freezes the dividend at $9.28. The bull increases it from $9.75 to $11.80 as recovery strengthens. Annual dividends climbed from $5.60 to $8.73 over the supplied period, while management forecasts $8,000 million of 2026 dividends and at least $20.50 of adjusted EPS.

blocks.heading: Is UnitedHealth's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: From 2021 through 2025, operating activities generated approximately $121.5 billion. This is cash collected and paid through operations, not the same thing as accounting earnings. Acquisitions consumed $54,332 million, while property, equipment and capitalized software consumed another $15,763 million. These investments expanded pharmacies, clinics and technology, but the Brazil exit and Change Healthcare disruption show why expansion alone is not evidence of success.

Shareholders received $33,481 million in dividends and $34,545 million through buybacks, in which the company purchases its own shares. In 2025, those payouts exceeded reported earnings, although operating cash was higher. That was possible because earnings include noncash expenses and estimates, while cash flow reflects collection and payment timing.
**Paid out more than it earned** — Year-end charges of $1,622 million made payouts exceed earnings by $1,405 million; without them, UnitedHealth would instead have kept $217 million.

paragraphs.text: The base case gains support if the $20.50 adjusted EPS floor holds and earnings approach the 13% growth target while dividends and buybacks continue. The bull case gains weight during 2028–2029 if Optum Health reaches its targeted margin range, technology improves productivity, cash flow funds larger repurchases, and repeated results cause analysts to raise estimates.

blocks.heading: What has UnitedHealth guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Management says the higher earnings floor already includes investment late in 2026. Its longer-term growth target is therefore an ambition to turn the recovery into a repeatable business, not proof that one strong quarter will continue. Analysts must decide whether the remaining members are better priced and whether medical costs stay controlled.

blocks.heading: Did UnitedHealth keep its past guidance?

paragraphs.text: In July, Hemsley restored guidance of at least US$16.00, and the year ended at US$16.35. On October 13, 2026, DeVeydt raised the outlook to at least US$20.50. That is evidence of improvement, but it does not erase the original failure to recognize rising costs quickly enough.

blocks.heading: How have UnitedHealth revenue and profit trended?

paragraphs.text: September 2026 net income rose from $2.3 billion a year earlier to $4.1 billion, while revenue slipped from about $113.2 billion to $112.7 billion. Earning more on slightly less revenue is better evidence than merely processing more premium dollars.

The sequence also matters. December 2025 was depressed by concentrated year-end charges, while June and September 2026 improved. Across nine months, removing identified portfolio and restructuring effects still leaves operating earnings growth. The recovery therefore survives those adjustments, but it must now survive medical-cost pressure and membership reductions.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in UnitedHealth's next results?

paragraphs.text: The fuller outlook should show whether management’s growth signal survives a detailed budget. Investors should read the medical care ratio alongside the operating cost ratio: treatment costs must improve without modernization simply moving expense elsewhere.
